title: Geometric irreducibility is preserved by subalgebras and directed colimits
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. A commutative $k$-algebra means a commutative unital ring $A$ with a fixed unital homomorphism $k\to A$; it is called geometrically irreducible when the associated $k$-scheme $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-scheme-over-base] is geometrically irreducible [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. (1) Let $A,S$ be commutative $k$-algebras and $u:A\to S$ an injective unital ring homomorphism commuting with the maps from $k$. If $S$ is geometrically irreducible, then $A$ is geometrically irreducible. (2) Let $I$ be a nonempty small directed poset (every two elements have a common upper bound) and $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ a diagram of commutative $k$-algebras with transition maps preserving $k$. If each $A_i$ is geometrically irreducible, then its colimit $\varinjlim_i A_i$ in commutative $k$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] is geometrically irreducible. Transition maps need not be injective. No finite-generation or reducedness hypothesis is imposed.
